ahead.weekend: Then {day}, if we get that far
forecast.lead: Looking down the barrel of the week, and I'm being generous with the word looking.
Here's the outlook, such as it is.
Let's walk the week. Try not to make plans.
Now the week. It doesn't get kinder.
Seven days, in order of arrival.
humid.dry: Bone-dry air at {humidity}%, and your lips will crack before your patience does.
{humidity}% humidity. Static everywhere and a nosebleed by evening.
humid.oppressive: And {humidity}% humidity. The air's basically soup. You won't so much breathe as wade.
{humidity}% and heavy. Sweat won't dry, so it won't cool you. Slow down.
intro: Doppler Dex Rime, and this is the only DOOMCAST that still bothers to check.
Dex Rime here. Let's find out what the atmosphere's planning to do to you.
Dex Rime, DOOMCAST. Let's look at it honestly, since nobody else will.
This is the DOOMCAST. Dex Rime. The sky doesn't negotiate, but it does announce.
intro.afternoon: Afternoon, survivors. Dex Rime, DOOMCAST, halfway through another {season} the planet's clearly regretting.
You made it to midday. Let's see what the atmosphere's charging you for the rest of it.
Midday, Basin. Dex Rime. Here's what the rest of the day intends to charge you.
Afternoon. The morning's forecast held, which never happens. Dex Rime, DOOMCAST.
Half the day gone and the sky's only warming up. Dex Rime here.
intro.evening: Evening. Dex Rime with the DOOMCAST, because somebody has to tell you what's coming after dark.
Good evening. The sun's clocking out, and I've got the overnight bad news ready to go.
Evening, Coldwater. Dex Rime with the overnight and the week behind it.
Dex Rime, DOOMCAST. Sun's going, and I've got what comes after.
Evening. Whatever you got away with today, the night has its own terms. Dex Rime.
intro.morning: Morning, what's left of you. Doppler Dex Rime, DOOMCAST, and the sky's already made its mind up.
Rise and shine. Well, rise. This is the {season} outlook, and it owes you nothing.
Up early? Bold. Dex Rime here with the forecast the Bureau doesn't want narrated.
Morning. Dex Rime. The sky's been up longer than you and it's already in a mood.
It's early, it's {temp} degrees, and I've got seven days of bad news queued up. Dex Rime, DOOMCAST.
Whatever woke you, it wasn't the weather being kind. Dex Rime with the outlook.
intro.night: Still awake? Same. Dex Rime, DOOMCAST, graveyard edition. Here's the sky at this ungodly hour.
Night owls, insomniacs and fugitives, this is Dex Rime. The forecast doesn't sleep either.
Late one. Dex Rime. Sky's awake, so I am, so here we are.
Dex Rime, DOOMCAST, small hours edition. Nothing good happens out there at this temperature.
If you're up, you've got a reason. Here's the sky you'll be doing it under. Dex Rime.
outro: That's the DOOMCAST. The weather's still trying to kill you. I'm just the one who says so out loud.
Doppler Dex Rime. Stay sealed, stay indoors, stay suspicious of clear skies. Back to you.
That's your seven days. Dress for the worst of them. Rime, out.
That's the week. Dress for the worst day in it, not the one you liked. Rime, out.
Dex Rime. The sky told me, I told you. The rest is yours.
sky.acid: Acid. Not rain with a bad attitude. Acid, and it'll go through a coat and then through you.
Caustic, so sealed rainwear or four walls. There's no third answer.
The sky gone yellow and meaning it, on a {precip}% chance of the worst kind of wet.
Caustic, sealed gear only. A hood isn't a plan, and a jacket isn't a hood.
A {precip}% chance of acid. It gets in the seams first. Check your seams.
sky.blizzard: A full blizzard at {temp} degrees, and it feels like the end.
Whiteout conditions. If you can read this, you're indoors, and you should stay that way.
Blizzard, and this one kills the unprepared. Don't audition.
Blizzard, {wind} km/h of snow going sideways at {temp} degrees. A stay-put day.
Full whiteout. You won't find your way, and it won't wait for you to try.
sky.clear: Clear skies, and enjoy the exposure while the atmosphere pretends to be your friend.
Not a cloud in it, just wide-open sky and whatever's still falling out of it.
Clear, and suspiciously so. Trust nothing.
Clear from end to end. Checked it twice, because I don't trust it either.
Nothing in the sky but sky. Take the walk. You've earned one.
sky.cloudy: Cloud, plural, doing that oppressive committee thing they do.
Partly cloudy, and the sky can't commit, same as everyone.
Cloud cover at {temp} degrees, mood grey.
Broken cloud doing nothing in particular. A rare day off from the sky.
Half-covered and unbothered. Enjoy the indifference. It's the best forecast I sell.
sky.fog: Fog, with visibility down to arm's-lengths. Walk into things carefully out there.
Thick fog, and the city goes missing. Honestly it's an improvement.
Fog at {humidity}% humidity, and the distinct sense you're being followed.
Fog thick enough to lean on. Keep a hand on something you know.
Visibility gone. Anything could be out there, and statistically, something is.
sky.haze: Haze over everything, that flat grey soup we call air these days.
A dirty haze the whole way through. Breathe shallow, blink often.
Haze, and the skyline's a rumour.
Haze sitting low. The air's carrying something and it isn't oxygen.
Grey soup again. Old lungs, take the day off.
sky.ion: An ion storm. The air itself goes conductive and every circuit in the city holds its breath.
The grid dropping. Not might drop. Drops. Charge nothing and trust nothing with a battery in it.
Static building to a scream. If it's got a chip in it, it's already living on borrowed time.
Charged air. Nothing with a battery survives contact, and that includes the thing you're watching this on.
Ion conditions, so have a light with a wick and a room with a door.
sky.overcast: Full overcast, a lid on the whole city. No sky, just ceiling.
Overcast and staying that way. The sun's filed for absence.
Solid overcast. Bring your own light.
Lid on. No shadows, no sun, no idea what time it is until it's dark.
Grey top to bottom. Bring your own reason to go out.
sky.rain: A {precip}% chance of rain, because of course. Bring something waterproof that isn't your skin.
A {precip}% chance of rain, and not clean rain. Is it ever.
A {precip}% chance of rain, with puddles that have opinions.
A {precip}% chance of steady rain. Not the cleansing kind. There isn't a cleansing kind anymore.
A {precip}% chance of getting wet through, and whatever leaks, it'll find it.
sky.sleet: Sleet, the worst of both worlds, arriving sideways.
Half rain, half ice, all misery. A {precip}% chance of exactly that.
Sleet at {temp} degrees. Dress for betrayal.
Sleet, freezing on the way down and again on the way through your coat.
Ice in the rain, so roads, stairs and rooftops all turn on you.
sky.snow: Snow, pretty from a window and lethal from a doorway.
Snow at {temp} degrees, settling on everything that stops moving.
A {precip}% chance of snow, so layer up or become part of the scenery.
Snow, and it'll lie. {temp} degrees says it's not going anywhere.
Steady snow. Warm boots or a short walk. Pick before you're out in it.
sky.storm: A proper storm. Wind, water, and the power grid holding its breath.
The whole system dropping on us at once, {wind} km/h and climbing.
Storm-force everything, so tie down what you love.
Everything at once, {wind} km/h, sheeting rain, and a grid that has opinions about all of it.
A storm sitting right on top of us and not moving. Batten what you can reach.
sky.thunderstorm: Thunderstorms rolling through. If you can count the gap to the thunder, you're too close.
A {precip}% chance of thunderstorms, which is a {precip}% chance of the sky picking a target.
Thunderstorms, so mind the metal roofs and the unlucky people. Stay clear of both.
Storm cells building. Lightning's the honest part. It's the wind that gets people.
A {precip}% chance of thunder. If your hair stands up, you've run out of time to move.
temp.cold: A biting {temp} degrees. Every gap in your coat is a mistake you'll feel.
{temp} and cold enough to bite. Keep moving or keep warm. Pick one.
{temp} and cutting. The wind finds whatever you left open.
{temp}. Cold enough that a wet coat becomes a real problem by hour two.
temp.cool: {temp} degrees, cool and grey. Jacket weather, if you own a jacket.
A cool {temp}. Not cruel, just unwelcoming. The city's default setting.
{temp}. Grey and grudging. Layer once and forget about it.
Cool at {temp}, the Basin's resting face.
temp.frigid: {temp} degrees. Your extremities are officially on their own out there.
{temp}, and that's not weather, that's a warning. Exposed skin freezes fast.
{temp}. Skin goes numb before it goes white, and numb is the part you'll ignore.
{temp} degrees. Cover the ears, cover the fingers, cover the fact you're out at all.
temp.hot: {temp} degrees and hot. Hydrate, stay shaded, and don't touch the metal.
A hard {temp}. The pavement's cooking. So are you, slower.
{temp}. Metal burns, tar softens, tempers go early.
Hot at {temp}. Water before you're thirsty, shade before you're dizzy.
temp.mild: A frankly suspicious {temp} degrees. Enjoy it, distrust it.
{temp} and mild, and the atmosphere's clearly planning something. It always is.
{temp}. Nothing wrong with it, which is itself a little unsettling.
Mild at {temp}. Do the errands today, because tomorrow may not offer.
temp.scorching: {temp} degrees. Scorching. This is heatstroke weather. Treat the sun as hostile.
{temp}. That's not summer, that's an oven with a schedule. Stay inside if you can.
{temp}. That is a hostile number. Midday isn't survivable in the open for long.
{temp} degrees. The city holds it all night. Indoors will be worse than out by two in the morning.
temp.warm: A warm {temp} degrees. Almost pleasant, if you don't think about why.
{temp} and climbing into comfortable. Savour it before it curdles.
{temp} and pleasant, which the Basin usually charges for.
Warm at {temp}. Windows open, guard up.
today.lead: Starting with what's waiting the second you step outside
First the here and the now
Today, before we get to the week
Conditions right now, and I do mean conditions
trend.clearing: Here's the good news, and I choke saying it. The wet clears as the week runs on.
It dries out toward the weekend. Briefly. Don't get attached.
Clears as it goes. Take the back half of the week for anything outdoors.
trend.cooling: It's all downhill. We shed heat from {hiTemp} to {loTemp} before the week's out. Dig out the layers.
Cooling trend. {loTemp} degrees is where this week is dragging us.
{hiTemp} down to {loTemp} by the far end. Find your layers before you need them.
trend.deteriorating: It gets worse. {severeCount} severe days ahead, {worstDay} the worst of them. Plan around it or pay for it.
Deteriorating fast. {severeCount} days flagged severe this week, and {worstDay}'s the one to fear.
{severeCount} severe days queued, {worstDay} the worst. Move what you can off it.
trend.steady: Steady as a flatline the whole week, same grey, same grind. Consistency, at least.
No real change ahead. The sky's found its rut and it's staying in it.
Same sky all week. The Basin at its most reliable, which is not a compliment.
trend.warming: Trend's upward, {loTemp} today crawling toward {hiTemp} by week's end. Make of that what you will.
It warms as the week goes. {hiTemp} degrees waiting at the far side.
Warms through the week, {loTemp} to {hiTemp}. It won't last. It never does.
warn.acid: Acid warning for {day}, and I'll say it twice if I have to. This is the one that takes skin off. Sealed rainwear, or you stay in.
It rains acid {day}. I'm not being colourful. Cover every inch or don't go out at all.
There's a caustic front {day}. It eats coats, it eats gear, and then it starts on you. You've had a week's notice.
Caustic {day}. Sealed rainwear, taped seams, or four walls. Nothing else works.
warn.blizzard: Whatever you had planned for {day}, cancel it. Thermal gear or a will, and that's the whole choice.
Blizzard warning for {day}. A {feels}-degree windchill. This one takes stragglers.
Expect whiteout {day}, with a {feels} windchill. Don't travel. There's no errand worth it.
warn.cold: Bundle up {day}. {temp} degrees will stop your heart if the muggers don't.
That's a cold warning for {day}. Thermal gear isn't optional. It's the difference.
Call {day} a cold-injury day. {temp} degrees. Fingers and toes go first, and they go quietly.
warn.generic: Take {day} seriously. The numbers say severe, and the numbers don't flatter.
It scores severe {day}. That's the instrument talking, not me.
warn.heat: Heat warning for {day}. {temp} degrees. Shade, water, and don't be a hero at noon.
We bake at {temp} degrees {day}. Heatstroke's free and quick. Decline it.
That's {temp} degrees {day}. Heat takes the fit and the young too. Nobody's exempt.
warn.ion: Ion storm {day}. The grid goes down and stays down. Anything electronic on you gets cooked.
Pulse warning for {day}. Leave the deck at home, leave the tablet in a shielded bag, and if you're chromed, sit down first.
Hard warning for {day}. Lights out citywide. Have a torch that doesn't need a circuit and a room you trust.
Ion conditions {day}. Everything with a circuit is a write-off. Unplug what you love.
warn.storm: Storm warning for {day}. Lightning, wind, and a grid that might not hold. Stay in.
The whole storm lands {day}. Charge what you can now, because power isn't promised.
Storm cells {day}, {wind} km/h, and a grid I wouldn't rely on. Charge it tonight.
warn.wind: Wind warning for {day}, {wind} km/h of it. Stay off the rooftops and away from the glass.
Gale-force gusts {day}. If it can fall on you, assume it will.
That's {wind} km/h {day}. Whole sheets of the Basin come loose at that speed.
wind.calm: Dead calm, too, not a breath of wind, which fog and worse just love.
No wind at all, which lets whatever's in the air just sit on the city.
wind.gale: A {wind} km/h gale on top of it. Lean into it and pray your boots hold.
{wind} km/h of gale. Scaffolding, signage, anybody light. All of it's in play.
wind.strong: Strong winds at {wind} km/h. Anything not bolted down is now airborne inventory.
{wind} km/h. Doors get away from you at this speed. Mind your fingers.
wind.windy: Add a {wind} km/h wind to file the warmth right off you.
There's a steady {wind} km/h behind it, so mind the loose signage.
{wind} km/h steady, and it'll take the warmth right off you.
